sources: Science Friday, The Marvelous, Misunderstood Lives Of Common Spiders (L. J. Young, quoting entomologist Dr. Eleanor Spicer Rice): on another spider's web the cellar spider (Pholcus phalangioides) places its legs on the edges and trembles like a trapped insect (aggressive mimicry); the owner comes out for the meal; the cellar spider tosses silk over it, wraps it up, eats it, then moves into the web and eats what got snagged; it also eats other spiders; https://www.sciencefriday.com/articles/the-marvelous-misunderstood-lives-of-common-spiders/

British Arachnological Society, Pholcus phalangioides: feeds on other spiders that come in range, including its own kind; long legs let it throw silk at prey from a distance; https://britishspiders.org.uk/node/26507
